title: Attachment-aware token normalization and reconciliation for compressed streaming
creator: Diego Alvarez
description:
Problem summary:

We observed recurring discrepancies between charged token counts and downstream model-side tokenization for streaming requests that include compressed or base64-encoded attachments (images, small binary blobs, or multi-part client-encoded payloads). Differences arise from: canonicalization differences (clients send slightly different encodings), server pre-processing (unpacking/compression), and tokenizer edge cases introduced by attachment boundary markers. These discrepancies surface as underbilling or overbilling on customer invoices and trigger manual investigations.

This ticket aims to design, implement, and validate an attachment-aware canonicalization and reconciliation layer in the metering pipeline so that token counts attributed to streaming sessions match a deterministic canonical tokenizer projection used for billing and audits. We must maintain low latency for hot paths, preserve streaming partial-credit semantics, and be resilient to out-of-order fragments and reconnects.

Goals:
- Ensure deterministic token count attribution for streams containing attachments or client-encoded sub-payloads.
- Preserve existing prefix-caching and KV semantics for text-heavy streams.
- Avoid changing customer-observed model responses; apply canonicalization only for billing/audit projection.
- Provide audit traces and metrics to detect remaining drift; enable automated alerting when drift > 0.1% across sampled traffic.
proposed_solution:
Design overview:

1) Attachment canonicalizer: Introduce a lightweight pre-metering canonicalization step that normalizes common client-side encodings into a single canonical form used only for token projection. For known encodings (base64, gzip, multipart delimiters) we normalize whitespace, strip non-semantic delimiters, and replace binary payloads with deterministic length markers (e.g., "<BLOB:len=NNN>"). This preserves semantic tokenization costs while avoiding tokenizer-dependent variance.

2) Stream checkpoints and deterministic fragments: At segment boundaries we compute and persist a canonicalization checkpoint (hash + canonical token offset). Checkpoints are used for idempotent resume and reconciliation on reconnects.

3) Tokenizer shadow-run: For a subset of traffic and during rollout, run the canonical billing tokenizer in shadow (no impact on runtime path) to measure divergence to the model-facing tokenizer. Collect metrics and sample diffs into a secure audit bucket.

4) Reconciliation job: Implement an hourly reconciliation job that compares produced credits vs. canonical projection for sessions with attachments. On mismatches beyond threshold, create automated billing-review tickets and emit an SLO alert.

5) Fast path optimization: For short responses (<512 tokens) bypass heavy canonicalization by applying a best-effort normalization to avoid extra CPU on the hot path.

Safety and backwards compatibility:
- This layer only affects billing projection; model inputs to runtime kernels stay unchanged.
- Migration is staged: enable canonicalizer for internal traffic, then shadow for production, then enable for billing for new customers, and finally for all customers after 4-week monitoring window.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce canonicalizer library integrated into pre-metering stage and unit-tested for known encodings
Persistable segment checkpoints available in metering store for resume/reconciliation
Shadow-tokenizer metrics show <0.1% divergence on sampled no-attachment traffic and explainable divergence for attachment cases
Reconciliation job flags sessions where billed tokens differ from canonical projection by >2 tokens or >0.5% and creates investigation artifacts
E2E perf regression < 2% p50 token-latency on streaming hot-path after fast-path optimization
tests:
Planned test matrix:

- Unit: canonicalizer normalization cases (base64 variations, gzip headers, CRLF vs LF multipart), deterministic marker insertion, checkpoint hashing.
- Integration: end-to-end simulated client sending multipart fragmented streams with reorders, disconnect/resume, and retries; assert final billed tokens == canonical projection.
- Load: run streaming synthetic suite with mixed payloads (90% text, 10% attachments) and validate latency impact under 95th percentile.
- Regression: compare monthly bill analytics on shadow rollout footprint to prior baseline to detect billing delta.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flags: add flags to toggle canonicalization (off|shadow|billing) per-customer and per-pool.
2) Internal alpha: enable 'shadow' for internal traffic and run reconciliation job immediately to gather diffs (2 weeks).
3) Beta customers: opt-in billing canonicalization for low-variance customers (2–4 weeks).
4) Full rollout: enable for all new customers; keep shadow for legacy customers for 4 more weeks; finally flip billing for all after perf and divergence SLOs met.
5) Post-rollout: run monthly drift reports and adjust canonicalization rules as new client encodings are observed.
